name: James Bond (Card Game)
description: James Bond is a high-speed, frantic card game that tests memory and reaction time. Unlike turn-based games, everyone plays simultaneously. Each player manages several 'books' (piles) of cards, racing to turn each book into a set of four-of-a-kind by swapping cards with a shared central pool. The first player to complete all their sets and shout 'James Bond!' wins.

history.origins: A variation of children's 'Speed' and 'Spoons' games. The name likely comes from the '007' high-stakes imagery and the intense, rapid pace of the game.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Derived from traditional real-time matching games.
1980s: Gained popularity as a common travel and camp game under various names (Lemon, Atlantis).
Present: A staple 'fast' card game used for quick entertainment and competitive reflex training.
history.cultural: Commonly known as 'Lemon' or 'Chanhassen' in different regions; universally appreciated for its lack of downtime.
history.evolution: The game's rules remain fairly constant, but regional variations in the number of books and cards in the 'pond' exist.

setup.players:
- 2 players: 24 cards each (6 books of 4).
- 3 players: 16 cards each (4 books of 4).
- 4 players: 12 cards each (3 books of 4).
setup.dealing: Deal all cards into piles of 4, leaving exactly 4 cards face-up in the center (the 'Pond').

rules.objective: Be the first player to have four-of-a-kind in all of your books and shout 'James Bond!'.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players start simultaneously at the signal 'Go!'.
2. You may pick up and look at ONE of your books at a time.
3. **Swapping**: You can swap one card from your book with one card from the Pond. You must place your card face-up in the Pond before taking the new one.
4. You cannot have more or fewer than 4 cards in your hand/book at any time.
5. You can put down a book and pick up another at any point to continue swapping.

Winning condition: Be the first player to have four-of-a-kind in all of your books and shout 'James Bond!'.

strategy.basic: Memory is key. Remember which cards are in your other books so when a useful card appears in the Pond, you know exactly which book to pick up.
strategy.intermediate: Blocking: If you see your opponent is hoarding 7s, keep a 7 in your current book to prevent them from finishing their set.
strategy.advanced: Dual-Processing: Skilled players can track the contents of 2-3 books simultaneously, swapping cards in rapid succession between the Pond and their books with almost no pause.
tips: Don't get tunnel-visioned on one book. If the Pond doesn't have what you need, check your other books immediately.
If you win, shout 'James Bond!' loudly to stop the other players from continuing.

variations.name: Book announcement
variations.description: Some players say 'book' each time they complete a pile of four equal cards, and 'book, James Bond' when they complete the last pile. Saying 'book' is not required and may give away information.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No engine constant overrides; announcement is optional verbal only.

variations.name: Win-call name
variations.description: The word used to claim a win varies by region: James Bond, Chanhassen, Atlantis, or the name of the game in other versions.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: No engine overrides; affects only the call phrase.

variations.name: Multi-card trade
variations.description: Some groups allow more than one card to be traded simultaneously (e.g. grab both fours at once in exchange for two cards from the pile).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Standard rules allow one card per exchange; this variant relaxes that.
